memo.verdict: Neutral; park. Coca-Cola HBC (CCH-GB) is a clean, well-understood case for a fair return, not a compelling one for the 20% bar: at 50.67 EUR (43.60 GBP; 4360.0 as quoted) the modal path returns about 12% a year over eighteen months and about 14% a year over three years at a held 24-month-forward multiple of 14.3x, and clears the bar only on a re-rating toward the ten-year median of 15.6x that needs the CCBA deal delivered and the naira and Egyptian pound calm at the same time, a joint outcome the record puts at about 35%. Conviction medium: the analysis is well-evidenced and the return is the issue, not the understanding. Price alarm at about 45.6 EUR (about 39.2 GBP), 10% below today, where the modal path alone returns 20% a year over eighteen months; event alarms at the November 2026 Q3 trading update and the CCBA close in H2 2026. The gate line does not force the park: management A, business quality B, predictability ('Transmission') B, trackability ('Leading indicators') B; the park is on the return against the bar. What turns it to progress: the price reaching the entry level with the earnings path intact, or a first CCBA half (H1 2027) showing accretion above the guided low single digits with the currencies calm. Invalidate levels: a 24-month-forward multiple below 12.0x on unchanged earnings; the company's own pair of organic gross margin below 36.5% with Emerging-segment volume growth below 2.0%; a concurrent 15% devaluation of both currencies in a quarter with Emerging EBIT margin down more than 100 basis points.
case: - The thesis in the record's words: Coca-Cola HBC is a top-decile bottler using an under-geared balance sheet to make a step-change in its perimeter, and at 50.67 EUR the shares pay a fair return for that, not a compelling one. The company is better than its return at today's price.

- The change is internal, broad and real, and the largest a bottler can make short of a merger: the CCBA acquisition (75% for US$2.6bn at about 10x EV to 2024 EBITDA; 14 markets; 493 million people; second-largest Coca-Cola bottler); the balance sheet used, not talked about (0.7x to about 1.6x; EUR 2.1bn of bonds; bridge cancelled); guidance raised as a repeated pattern; standards improvement A (portal orders 15.4% of the total in 2025 from 11.5%; 47% of Nigerian volume digital; NPS 78 from 66; comparable gross margin +350 basis points FY2022 to FY2025; return on invested capital 11.1% to 19.4%); strategy shifted from bolt-ons of about EUR 150m a year to a transformational step, articulated and resourced. What is absent is a chief-executive change; the chief executive's record since December 2017 is the foundation the case rests on, not a change force.

- The external forces are a net tailwind for now, but the largest is the pause of a structural headwind: demand B (group volume +7.5%; emerging-market per-capita consumption four to forty times below developed benchmarks; the European part weather-assisted), competition B (share +80 basis points, a sixth consecutive year; the Egyptian gap to PepsiCo closed from 13 points to 5; where it tightens: South Africa with Varun Beverages after the close; buying groups), disruption B (zero sugar, energy and digital ordering turned to advantage; GLP-1 a limited threat on Redburn's reading), own cycle B (from inflation-led pricing to volume-led growth), supply side C (over 85% hedged for FY2026; unit-cost guidance raised), political and regulatory C (deposit schemes; an Italian sugar excise of EUR 0.10 a litre from January 2027; rPET premium EUR 55m), macro C (translation turned from a EUR 0m to 30m headwind to a EUR 0m to 10m tailwind; the naira at NGN 1,563 to 1,606 per euro in H1 2026 against 1,705 at end-2025; Egypt's urban CPI re-accelerated to 14.9%; translation drag averaged 3.8% of sales a year over 2019 to 2024).
counter_case: - At its strongest: the market has priced this company correctly. It is a 10% compounder, not a 15% one, and at 14x to 17x forward earnings it earns its holders a fair 12% to 14% a year and no more. The second-half deceleration is demand, not habit: unit-cost guidance was raised to low-to-mid single digits, Q4 has four fewer selling days, and Developing-segment margins are already down 70 basis points under marketing spend. The deal raises risk faster than return: a 7.4% EBITDA-margin asset, fourteen new currencies, 25% minorities, a 5.47% share issue, capital intensity toward 8% of sales and the buyback gone; low-single-digit first-year accretion is the whole of what the company will commit to, and no long-term return target is disclosed. The transactional currency mismatch (64% of revenue in emerging-market currencies against dollar-priced concentrate and packaging, with USD revenue of 1.2%) is the highest among soft-drink peers, and Egypt's macro is deteriorating. The multiple has just shown, by falling 16% in seven weeks on no estimate change, that it can go down as easily as up; the sell-side's bear cases are 2,200p at 12.4x (Morgan Stanley) and 3,000p (Jefferies). Every number in this hypothesis is real and in the evidence.

- Against the foundations: they are a bottler's, not a compounder's, and the precedent is one market. The brand owner takes the concentrate margin (60% to 70% gross) and sets concentrate prices at its discretion; comparable EBIT margin is 11.7%, gross margin 36.8%, cash conversion about 70%; the runway is capital expenditure at 7% to 8% of sales, not 20%. Translation drags of 6.2% and 8.2% in 2023 and 2024 show what the mismatch does, and above a 30% move the hedging corridor breaks. CCBA's assets are worse than Egypt's were, the operator's bandwidth is being stretched across fourteen territories at once, and the market is not rewarding staples or bottlers now.
triggers: - Price: about 45.6 EUR (about 39.2 GBP) over eighteen months, or 43.4 EUR (about 37.4 GBP) over three years, is the entry level at which the modal path clears 20% a year; reaching it with the earnings path intact turns the park to progress.

- The November 2026 Q3 trading update: settles whether the second half is habit or demand; alarm if second-half organic EBIT growth is below 1%, H2 comparable EPS below 1.41 EUR, Emerging-segment volume growth below 2%, or organic gross margin contracting; the sell-side expects a second beat-and-raise of 1% to 3%; alarm on any EPS cut of 2% or more.

- The CCBA close (H2 2026; the South African Tribunal's final hearing in Q3 or Q4 2026): alarm if Tribunal conditions delay the close beyond 2026 or if capital expenditure runs above 8% of sales; the first consolidated half (H1 2027, August 2027) invalidates the deal leg if CCBA's margin is below 7%, and moves the modal multiple toward 15.6x if accretion is above the guided low single digits with the currencies calm.

- Currencies: alarm at a parallel-rate premium above 10% on the naira or the Egyptian pound; invalidate at a concurrent 15% devaluation of both in a quarter with Emerging EBIT margin down more than 100 basis points; a 20% single-currency devaluation costs about 3 points of EPS growth and would take 'Modal return' to F on the eighteen-month view.

- The multiple: invalidate at a 24-month-forward multiple below 12.0x on unchanged earnings, which would say the market has decided the deal is dilutive; a prudent trough is 12.0x, and the framework's scepticism says plan for 10.5x.
- The company's own invalidation pair: organic gross margin below 36.5% with Emerging volume growth below 2.0%.
